header:
Date: 2025-10-21
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~43 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Ruth Palmer (Helios CTO), Anil Mehra (Helios Infra Lead), Tiffany Gomez (Helios Security), Jonas Li (Helios ML)
Artifacts shared: redwood-pilot-checklist.pdf (link), bench-results-template.xlsx (link), security-whitepaper_v3.pdf (link)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on gating for private deployment network provisioning and access. Main topics: VPC peering details, CIDR allowlist, preliminary latency benchmarks on dev infra, SOC2 / HIPAA clarifications, and next steps for canary deployment. Agreement to run a focused 1k-request benchmark and to exchange security/network artifacts. Some minor transcription errors in meeting notes; technical deep-dive planned for next week if bench results show tail-latency issues.
topics: 1) Env gating & network provisioning status; 2) Benchmark plan and metrics (p50/p95/p99); 3) Security/compliance items (KMS, audit logs, data residency); 4) Dedicated vs hosted throughput; 5) Next steps and owners
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): All right, everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:09] Ruth: Ruth here.
[00:11] Anil: Anil, yep.
[00:13] Tiffany: Tiffany on secure and compli—compliance.
[00:16] Jonas: Jonas, ML.
[00:18] Samir (SE): Samir, Redwood SE. Diego from CSM is also on.
[00:22] Maya: Cool. Agenda is network gating, bench plan, and security blockers. We'll keep this tight, 30–45 minutes.
[00:30] Ruth: Sounds good.
[00:32] Maya: Quick status from Helios on infra—Anil?
[00:36] Anil: Yeah, so we've completed the initial infra VPCs, we've got a transit gateway, but we still need the allowlist IPs for the Redwood dedicated pool and confirmation on outbound egress. We had a question about whether Redwood needs a peering or if a NAT/egress path is fine.
[00:48] Samir: Right, so for the pilot we recommend VPC peering with the private control plane (if you're going Dedicated) or a managed egress for Hosted. Peering gives lower latency, less NAT jitter, but adds some routing configuration on your side.
[01:05] Anil: Okay, peering makes sense. Is there a CIDR overlap risk? Our CIDR ranges are pretty broad across prod and staging.
[01:14] Maya: We sent our recommended CIDR ranges in the pilot checklist, but I can resend. The key is no overlap; if overlap exists we can proxy via transit.
[01:27] Jonas: Quick question on KV cache—sorry, K-V cache—are we storing prefixes inside Helios or is that on Redwood? Just trying to understand data flow for PHI.
[01:37] Samir: Good call. So by default KV cache (we sometimes call it KV cash in docs, sorry) is ephemeral and stays in the serving tier; for Private Dedicated we can set cache affinity inside your VPC. PHI should not be persisted beyond the request unless you opt-in to caching.
[01:54] Tiffany: So HIPAA concern: does Redwood encrypt KV cache with our KMS keys? We need customer-managed keys for anything that touches PHI.
[02:03] Samir: Yes, for Private we support customer KMS/HSM via our KMS integration. That ties into our audit logs. We'll attach the whitepaper.
[02:12] Tiffany: Please do. Also need an explanation of retention windows and audit log formats.
[02:18] Diego (CSM): I'll put the security addendum in the shared drive after this call.
[02:22] Ruth: On benchmarks—Jonas, can you remind the team of what we're shooting for as success criteria?
[02:29] Jonas: Sure. For interactive clinician flows it's <150ms median and <400ms p95 on 256 token sequences. Cost target is under $0.002 per call for typical prompts.
[02:41] Maya: Noted. Samir, you had a bench plan?
[02:44] Samir: Yes, we'll run a 1k-request synthetic load across the dev endpoint that mirrors your prompt size distribution. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and GPU utilization. We'll test both Hosted-ish routing and Dedicated-like peered path if we can.
[02:59] Anil: If we do peering we want to see how tail latency behaves during parallel requests. Our main worry is noisy neighbors.
[03:08] Samir: Absolutely. We'll run bursty patterns and steady-state. Also will test cold-starts and warm path with KV cache enabled.
[03:19] Maya: Can we get that by Friday?
[03:21] Samir: Yes, Friday EOD looks doable.
[03:24] [03:24] Jonas: Are you going to use our dev VPC or Redwood's sandbox?
[03:29] Samir: We'll run both: first Redwood's sandbox to baseline then we'll route to your dev environment once network allowlist is configured.
[03:37] Ruth: About allowlist, Anil will supply CIDR and firewall contact by end of week.
[03:42] Anil: Yes, I'll get that to you.
[03:44] [03:44] Maya: Great. Security—Tiffany, main blockers?
[03:48] Tiffany: We need KMS architecture, proof of SOC2 coverage for private control plane, and clarification about log retention in the console. Also SSO integration—do you support SAML?
[03:58] Maya: We support SAML/SSO and RBAC on the Console. SOC2 we are covered; I'll link the attestation and the SOC2 addendum which details Private deployment controls.
[04:10] Tiffany: Perfect. Also audit log format—JSON structured logs or CSV?
[04:15] Samir: JSON structured, with fields for request id, model, token counts, timestamps — can export to your SIEM.
[04:24] Ruth: What's the plan for data residency? We have EU patients, need regional routing.
[04:29] Maya: We can route requests to region-specific pools; for Private we can run entirely inside your VPC in EU region. We'll note that in the security doc.
[04:38] Jonas: One more thing on model variants — do you have quantized variants that trade quality for cost? We want to test a smaller variant for batch inference.
[04:46] Samir: Yes, Redwood catalog includes quantized builds and we can recommend quant profiles per workload. We'll include recommended profiles in the bench report.
[04:56] Anil: For network, do you need inbound ports open from our side, or is it only egress?
[05:02] Samir: Typically egress with allowlist is fine. For peering you configure routing; we don't need you to open inbound ports unless you're exposing endpoints.
[05:12] Maya: We're about 12 minutes in. Any new blockers on your side?
[05:16] Ruth: Nothing new.
[05:18] Tiffany: One ask — show us an example audit log snippet with PHI redaction markers.
[05:25] Samir: Will include redacted sample in the security addendum.
[05:30] [05:30] Diego: Also wanted to confirm ownership for the canary deploy checklist — we'll run that with Helios ops.
[05:36] Maya: Diego and Anil will pair on that. We'll schedule a 60-minute canary walkthrough next week.
[05:44] Anil: Works for me.
[05:46] Jonas: Back to benchmarks — what hardware will you be using for dedicated dev? Gpus?
[05:52] Samir: For Dedicated pilot it's A100-equivalent nodes; for Hosted we have mixed fleet. Bench will note device types and kernel profiles.
[06:01] Jonas: Please include token throughput numbers per GPU.
[06:05] Samir: Will do.
[06:07] Maya: Any risk of cost spike if we run large batch experiments?
[06:12] Samir: We'll provide an estimated cost delta in the bench spreadsheet and run a couple of controlled runs. You can also set spending alerts.
[06:21] Ruth: Great. On contractual items — procurement asked about SLAs for Dedicated pilot, can we get a short-term SLA?
[06:29] Maya: We offer SLA-backed Dedicated contracts but for pilot we can provide target uptime and a short support commitment, not full enterprise SLA until procurement completes. I'll have contract ops draft a pilot addendum.
[06:41] Tiffany: Will that include incident response times?
[06:44] Maya: Yes, we'll include an on-call contact and response window for priority incidents.
[06:49] [06:49] Anil: I got a note — do you support mutual TLS for the control plane?
[06:54] Samir: Mutual TLS is supported for Private and Dedicated control planes; we'll document the cert rotation process.
[07:02] Jonas: Any plan for monitoring model regressions during pilot?
[07:07] Diego: Redwood Optimize ties evals and regressions to your prompt sets. We can set up a baseline eval run as part of the pilot.
[07:16] Jonas: Good — please include that.
[07:20] Maya: Okay, let's recap action items. Samir?
[07:24] Samir: I'll run the 1k-request bench on Redwood sandbox and then on Helios dev once allowlist is up; upload results + profile sheet to the shared drive by Friday 2025-10-24.
[07:37] Maya: Tiffany?
[07:39] Tiffany: I'll share the KMS diagram and compliance checklist by 2025-10-28.
[07:45] Anil: I'll provide CIDR and firewall contacts by 2025-10-28.
[07:50] Maya: Maya will send pilot pricing estimate and a short pilot contract addendum by 2025-10-23.
[07:57] Ruth: Can we schedule the canary walkthrough for 2025-10-28 at 16:00 UTC?
[08:04] Diego: I'll send invite now.
[08:07] [08:07] Jonas: One small nit — in previous docs we saw references to "Redwood-verified models" spelled wrong as "Redwood varified" which created some confusion; if you could standardize naming in the doc set that helps.
[08:20] Maya: Noted, we'll clean up.
[08:23] Tiffany: Also, please call out redaction approach for logs so our privacy team can sign off.
[08:29] Samir: We'll include sample redacted logs and the export schema.
[08:33] Ruth: Is there anything blocking the bench right now?
[08:36] Samir: Only the allowlist; if Anil sends CIDR we can run the dev-targeted runs immediately.
[08:42] Anil: On it.
[08:44] Maya: Cool. Any other questions?
[08:47] [08:47] Jonas: None from me.
[08:49] Tiffany: No.
[08:51] Ruth: All good.
[08:53] Maya: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the docs and bench results.
[09:00] [09:00] End of call.

Note: transcript contains occasional speech-to-text artifacts (e.g., 'KV cash' for KV cache, 'varified' for verified). Some timestamps are approximate.
